A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MIO and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Content can be matched reliably despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original MIO benchmark evaluations, tokenizer comparisons, training loss curves, generated examples, and human evaluations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental and human-evaluation results, independently of its newly reported third-party leaderboard scores.

M1.justification: Both versions retain Yi-6B initialization, SEED and speech tokenization, sequential speech-token generation, masked packing, next-token prediction, three pre-training stages, and supervised fine-tuning. No procedural or architectural change is established.

E1.justification: v4 adds MME-Unify's broad evaluation suite, extending coverage to scenarios including fine-grained image reconstruction, SpotDiff, auxiliary-line reasoning, and questions with image answer options. Existing training datasets and image, speech, video, language, and OmniBench evaluations remain.

E2.justification: New Table 2 compares against Gemini2.0-flash-exp, Anole, VILA-U, Janus-Pro, Janus-Flow, Emu3, and Show-o, alongside SEED-LLaMA. Separately, Table 3 removes the previously reported Qwen-VL-Chat and LLaVA 1.5 comparisons, substantially revising comparative coverage.

E3.justification: The added MME-Unify evaluation introduces Overall, Understanding, Generation, and Unify metrics and describes image-option single-choice evaluation. Settings for retained experiments, including splits, training budgets, decoding parameters, and human-evaluation procedures, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The tokenizer comparison moves from Section 3.6 to Appendix E.6 but retains its 3K-step comparison and examples. OmniBench analysis, loss curves, human evaluations, and demonstrations are also retained. MME-Unify is additional benchmark evaluation, not a new ablation or robustness study.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same three-annotator human evaluations, averaging procedure, and 82.3% image-ranking agreement. No new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports MIO-Instruct scores of 37.2 Overall, 41.5 Understanding, 53.5 Generation, and 16.6 Unify: second overall and highest in generation among listed models. Existing MIO scores and appendix findings remain unchanged; Table 3 removes Qwen-VL-Chat and LLaVA 1.5 result entries.

T1.justification: Equation 1 retains the same autoregressive cross-entropy objective. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are substantively added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about four-modality understanding and generation, four-stage training, competitive performance, and interleaved generation capabilities. MME-Unify supplies additional evidence without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly attributes weak Unify performance to missing training examples with image answer options. A new Limitations section explicitly discusses speech/video data coverage, computational demands, evaluation gaps, and fixed-context constraints.

D1.justification: v4 removes the abstract's code/model availability statement and repository link, and omits the VQGAN-1024 compression rate of 16 from the relocated ablation description. Training hardware, hyperparameters, preprocessing, and prompts remain documented. These omissions do not establish changed implementation or actual resource withdrawal.

R1.justification: v4 adds references including MME-Unify, Janus-Pro, Qwen2.5-VL, Mavors, and VersaVid-R1, while removing coverage including ImageBind, OmniBind, InternVideo, and several earlier vision-language works. The central positioning of DIDO against alternative modeling approaches remains.

P1.justification: Related Works is condensed and its subsections merged; demonstration and tokenizer discussion move to Appendix E. Cross-references, affiliations, and wording are revised, and limitations and acknowledgments are added. Most method and results exposition remains intact.

P2.justification: The paper changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout, extensively reflowing tables, captions, and figures. It adds the MME-Unify table, moves the training table and tokenizer figure into the appendix, and removes Emu1's feature-table column. Existing illustration content is retained.

improvement.justification: MME-Unify adds quantitative checks of capabilities previously supported mainly by demonstrations, while the new failure explanation and limitations improve qualification of the claims. These modest gains are partly offset by removing informative Qwen-VL-Chat/LLaVA 1.5 comparisons and the repository pointer. The unchanged method and existing results do not establish improved model performance.
